H1_Commuter_Concentration.hypothesis: H1: Working days have a higher average share of daily rentals during peak commuting hours (07-09 and 17-19) than non-working days.
H1_Commuter_Concentration.statistical_interpretation: Reject H0 (p = 4.9998e-05). The difference of 25.4 percentage points (95% CI: [24.7%, 26.1%]) is statistically overwhelming.
H1_Commuter_Concentration.business_interpretation: On working days, 51.6% of all daily bike trips occur during just 6 hours (07-09 and 17-19). This extreme concentration creates severe directional tidal flows that deplete residential docks in the morning and flood downtown docks in the evening, explaining the perceived bike shortages.

H3_Temperature_Threshold.hypothesis: H3 (Exploratory): Daily rental volume differs on extreme hot days (mean temp >= 32C) vs other days.
H3_Temperature_Threshold.business_note: Not statistically significant (p = 0.209). Peak heat coincides with summer tourism, confounding a direct heat-suppression effect.
